title: Grateful Dead Live at Max Yasgur's Farm on 1969-08-16
lineage: SBD > MR (8trk Master Reels @ 15ips) > D > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with generally good clarity captures a historically‑significant Woodstock set highlighted by a soaring Dark Star and an epic Turn On Your Love Light, though the show is uneven (St. Stephen cut short) and littered with stage banter.
ai_review.review: The SBD source delivers a surprisingly crisp mix for a festival recording, letting listeners hear Jerry’s bell‑like guitar on Dark Star and Pigpen’s raw vocal power on the 45‑minute Love Light.  The performance is historically important but uneven – St. Stephen ends abruptly, technical glitches and Ken Babbs’ spoken‑word interludes interrupt several songs, and the overall flow feels chaotic.

ai_rating.rationale: Average star rating across >40 reviews is ~4.0; most reviewers praise the recording’s clarity and the standout Dark Star/Love Light while noting performance flaws, yielding a solid but not exceptional overall score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp mix comparable to other SBD releases; occasional audience bleed and minor drop‑outs noted, plus spoken‑word interruptions that some find distracting but do not mask the music.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set feels chaotic due to monitor problems, on‑stage babbling and technical hiccups; despite that the band delivers high energy jams, especially in the second half.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Guitar tone described as ringing like a bell and praised on Dark Star and Love Light.
band_member_comments.Bob: Pigpen’s vocal is strong on Love Light; some reviewers mention possible electrical shocks affecting his performance.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey’s drum kit is noted in later comments where equipment failure blew up near the drums.
